---
title: "Running the workflow"
---

## Running the pipeline

The main process -- `tar_make()` -- coordinates: it submits SLURM worker jobs through
crew.cluster and must stay alive until they finish, because workers connect back to it.

**As a batch job** (anything long, e.g. a full build):

```sh
sbatch run_pipeline.sbatch                                     # everything outdated
sbatch run_pipeline.sbatch 'tidyselect::starts_with("fit_")'   # fits only (no ingestion)
sbatch run_pipeline.sbatch 'tidyselect::starts_with("db_")'    # rebuild DB rows from stored results
tail -f logs/targets_main_<jobid>.out
```

The argument is passed to `tar_make(names = ...)`. targets builds the named targets plus
whatever they depend on, and nothing else, so a part of the pipeline can run without the long
fits. For example, the repeated-measures analysis alone for every dataset:

```sh
sbatch run_pipeline.sbatch 'c(starts_with("design_"), starts_with("expr_"), starts_with("norm_"),
  starts_with("vp_"), starts_with("dream_"), starts_with("de_tables_"), starts_with("dupcor_"),
  starts_with("composition_"), starts_with("controls_"), starts_with("control_factor_"),
  any_of("variance_explore"))'
```

Check `tar_outdated(names = ...)` with the same selection first: it lists exactly what would
build.

**From RStudio Server on the cluster**, open the project and use the console:

```r
library(targets)
tar_visnetwork()                            # the graph, outdated targets highlighted
tar_outdated()                              # what tar_make() would rebuild
tar_make()                                  # build everything outdated
tar_make(names = starts_with("fit_pca_"))   # a subset
tar_make(as_job = TRUE)                     # as an RStudio background job
tar_progress_summary()                      # progress while a run is going
```

An interactive session ends with its SLURM job (16 h at most on `interactive`), so long runs
belong in `run_pipeline.sbatch`.

**Reading results:** `tar_read(fit_pca_EARLI)` returns a target's value.
`read_method_fits("EARLI", "spca")` (`R/targets/run_method_fit.R`, available after
`targets::tar_load_globals()`) returns a method's fits as one `list(params, result)` per grid
row, both sPCA stages included.

## Targets per dataset

`R/targets/factories.R` builds these targets for each dataset `<key>` (the dataset id, made safe
for a name):

| Stage | Targets |
|---|---|
| inputs | `inputs_<key>` (file target over the config, preprocessing script and raw data), `meta_<key>`, `mat_<key>`, `mat_nn_<key>`, `sample_meta_<key>`, `subjects_<key>` (each matrix column's subject, `fit_subjects()`) |
| fits, per method `<m>` | `grid_<m>_<key>`, `fit_<m>_<key>` (one branch per batch of grid rows); sPCA adds `grid_spca_refine_<key>`, `fit_spca_refine_<key>`, `selection_spca_<key>` |
| ingestion, per method | `ingest_<m>_<key>`, `pairs_<m>_<key>`, `representatives_<m>_<key>`, `redundancy_<m>_<key>`, `fgsea_jobs_<m>_<key>`/`fgsea_<m>_<key>`, `icasso_ica_<key>`, `factor_vp_<m>_<key>` (score-level variance partition, when the dataset or its parent has a design) |
| repeated measures (datasets with a `design:` block; `R/targets/variance.R`) | `design_<key>`, `expr_<key>`, `norm_<key>`, `vp_<key>`, `dream_<key>`, `de_tables_<key>` (every contrast's table; the only reader of the dream fit), `dupcor_<key>` (time courses), `controls_<key>` (arrays with `control_probes`), `control_factor_<key>` (with `control_probes: {covariate: true}`), `composition_<key>`, `vp_explore_<key>`, `vp_summary_<key>`, `vp_qc_<key>` (plots and tables in `results/variance/<dataset>/`), `variance_files_<key>` |
| WGCNA | `wgcna_ora_jobs_`/`wgcna_ora_<key>`, `wgcna_fit_jobs_`/`wgcna_fit_diag_<key>`, `wgcna_dataset_diag_<key>` |
| per dataset | `metadata_files_<key>`, `matrix_file_<key>`, `matrix_diagnostics_<key>`, `ensembl_map_<key>`, `enrichment_<key>`, `factor_gene_files_<key>`, `drivers_<key>`, `db_<key>` |
| across datasets | `projectr_jobs_<key>`/`projectr_<key>`, `projection_scores_<key>`, `gene_space_<key>`, `db_cross_dataset`, `variance_explore`, plus `msigdb_pathways`, `db_schema`, `ensembl_maps`, `matrix_files`, `dataset_families`, `composition_markers` |

## What reruns when

targets reruns a target when its command, its inputs or a function it calls changes (comments
and whitespace don't count).

| Change | Reruns |
|---|---|
| a dataset's config, preprocessing script or raw files | that dataset only |
| a method's grid in one config (e.g. adding a rank) | only the new grid rows' fits, then that dataset's ingestion |
| a method's fit function or `<name>_registry` | every fit of that method (sPCA: about a day) |
| `run_method_fits()`, `fit_subjects()`, the grid helpers, `capture_fit()` | every fit of every method that uses them |
| a dataset's `design:` block, `R/lib/design.R` or `R/targets/variance*.R` | that dataset's repeated-measures targets and score-level partitions, then its DB write -- never a fit |
| a controller's `batch_size` or `cpus_per_task` | that method's fits (they change the grid) |
| a controller's memory, time or worker settings | nothing |
| a method's `<name>_ingest` or the ingestion code in `R/targets/` | ingestion and the DB writes only |
| `R/db/schema.sql` or `views.sql` | the DB writes (after deleting the DB, see [Database](database.qmd)) |

Stopping a run keeps every finished branch. Removing a dataset from `config/pipeline.yml` leaves
its results in the store (`targets::tar_prune()` deletes them).

## SLURM resources

Each method has a crew controller under `controllers:` in `config/pipeline.yml`: memory, CPUs,
wall time, idle timeout, `batch_size`, `tasks_max`. Ingestion, enrichment (`fgsea`), projections
(`projectr`) and matrix building (`prep`) have their own. Each controller grows its pool of
worker jobs with the backlog and shrinks it when work runs out; a worker is one SLURM job that
runs tasks until it's idle or reaches its time limits.

- **No worker caps by default.** SLURM's scheduler and per-user limits (200 running jobs per
  user on HTCF) decide what runs when; a controller without `workers:` is effectively uncapped.
  PCA, NMF and ICA keep small caps for efficiency: their tasks take seconds, much less than a
  worker's ~30 s R start-up, so one worker per task would mostly be start-up.
- **Batches.** Each branch costs the main process about a second of bookkeeping, so fast
  methods group grid rows into branches (`batch_size`), and projections run one branch per
  (source, target) dataset pair.
- **Backups for out-of-memory.** A controller's `backup:` block (crew backup controllers)
  retries a task whose worker crashed `crashes_max` times -- typically killed for exceeding
  memory on the largest datasets -- on `<name>_backup` with more memory.
- **One fit per worker for long fits.** sPCA and the `vp` controller (variancePartition and
  dream, BiocParallel `MulticoreParam` over `cpus_per_task`) use `tasks_max: 1`, so no long task
  starts late in a worker's life.

### Main-process memory

The main process's memory scales with the number of tasks it has handed to crew and not yet
collected, not with the data:

- **Every ready task is pushed at once.** targets pushes a ready target to its controller unless
  the controller is *saturated* (crew's `saturated()`: tasks pushed ≥ `workers`); a saturated
  controller's targets wait in targets' own backlog as names. Without a `workers:` cap a
  controller never saturates, so every ready task is pushed immediately, including the ones
  waiting in SLURM's queue behind the 200-running-jobs limit.
- **Each pushed task carries the globals.** The payload is the target plus every object and
  function that `_targets.R` and `R/` define: about 5.3 MB serialized (2026-10-14), mostly source
  references. `tar_source()` parses with `keep.source = TRUE`; without them it's 0.44 MB.
- **It's held in the main process.** mirai's dispatcher is a thread in the main R process
  (mirai ≥ 2.7), so each outstanding task costs about twice its payload, ~10.6 MB.

The full run's opening burst (2026-10-14: about 1,400 tasks, mostly CoGAPS, WGCNA and sPCA, as
every dataset's grids became ready together) took the main process to 14.75 GB within two
minutes, and 16.8 GB after twenty. That burst crashed a run with `--mem=16G`; `run_pipeline.sbatch` requests more, and
up to about 20 GB is acceptable on HTCF. The script also writes
`logs/targets_main_<jobid>_mem.tsv` (the job's memory, each process's RSS and the number of
worker jobs, every 30 s).

If it becomes a problem, shrink the payload rather than cap workers (a cap below the cluster's
running limit leaves capacity unused when one controller has the remaining work). The targets
manual recommends putting a large project's functions in an R package: each task then ships
only the package name, and workers load it. Sourcing `R/` without source references would also
cut the payload about twelvefold; targets hashes functions without them, so neither change
reruns anything.

### Tuning

Aim for about 75% average memory and CPU use, never below 50%, and err on the high side. Size
memory for the largest dataset (SHIP-TREND: 8,000 genes × 991 samples), not EARLI.

1. Run the method, e.g. `tar_make(names = starts_with("fit_nmf_"))`.
2. Find the worker array ids: `sacct -X -S <start> --format=JobID,JobName | grep crew-worker`.
3. Check usage with `seff <jobid>`, or for an array
   `python /scratch/mblab/chasem/seff-array/seff-array.py <array id>`. seff-array needs a
   terminal; from a non-interactive shell wrap it:
   `script -qc "stty cols 100; python .../seff-array.py <id>" /dev/null`.

**The `vp` controller also records its own use:** `norm_`, `vp_` and `dream_` store their job's
cgroup peak memory and CPU seconds in their result (`$resources`, `job_resources()` in
`R/targets/variance.R`), and `vp_summary_<key>` reports them. That was needed when these tasks
used socket (`SnowParam`) workers, which left the job's process tree so `seff` missed them;
since 2026-10-14 they use forked (`MulticoreParam`) workers, which use no ports and which `seff`
should count. Compare the two on the next run.

The current values and the measurements behind them are in `config/pipeline.yml`'s comments.

## Running on a scheduler other than SLURM

The pipeline has only run on SLURM (HTCF). The targets themselves don't depend on that: they
only name a controller (`tar_resources_crew(controller = "prep")` in `R/targets/factories.R`),
so the pipeline's logic is the same on any crew backend. Six things are tied to SLURM, and a
port would change these:

1. **Controller construction.** `build_controller_group()` (`R/targets/controllers.R`) is the
   only place controllers are built, and it calls `crew.cluster::crew_controller_slurm()` with
   `crew_options_slurm()`. The other [crew.cluster](https://wlandau.github.io/crew.cluster/)
   schedulers (SGE, PBS, LSF) have their own controller and options functions, and
   `crew::crew_controller_local()` runs everything on one machine (useful for tests).
2. **The `controllers:` block.** Its fields map onto SLURM: `time_minutes` is the job's `--time`
   (and sets the soft wall time, `seconds_wall`), `memory_gigabytes_required` and
   `cpus_per_task` are the job's resources, and `partition` (under `cluster:`) is the SLURM
   partition. Other schedulers name and limit these differently, and the comments in
   `config/pipeline.yml` reason about SLURM's behaviour (jobs killed for exceeding memory,
   per-user job limits).
3. **The worker environment.** `worker_script_lines()` (`R/targets/controllers.R`) puts R on
   each worker's PATH from the spack environment in the `cluster:` block, then changes into the
   project directory so renv activates. `cluster.setup_lines` replaces the spack lines with
   whatever provides R elsewhere.
4. **Starting the run.** `run_pipeline.sbatch` is a SLURM script that runs the `tar_make()`
   main process. Any way of keeping that process alive for the whole run works, because the
   workers connect back to it.
5. **Resource recording.** `job_resources()` (`R/targets/variance.R`) reads the job's cgroup
   (v2) under `slurmstepd.scope`, using `SLURM_JOB_ID`. Outside SLURM, or without cgroup v2, it
   returns no usable measurement; the `vp` tasks' `$resources` would be empty.
6. **Names and comments.** The method registries' `resource_defaults()` take an argument called
   `slurm_cfg` (only `cpus_per_task` is read from it), and comments and docs mention SLURM and
   HTCF throughout.

A port is therefore mostly a rewrite of `build_controller_group()` and the `controllers:`
fields, plus items 3 to 5. The resource numbers in `config/pipeline.yml` were tuned on SLURM and
would need tuning again.

## Logs and monitoring

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| main process | `logs/targets_main_<jobid>.out` |
| main-process memory | `logs/targets_main_<jobid>_mem.tsv` (every 30 s) |
| workers | `logs/crew/<controller>_<jobid>.out` |
| per-target errors and warnings | `tar_meta(fields = c(error, warnings))` |
| progress | `tar_progress_summary()`, `tar_poll()` |

A failed fit doesn't fail its branch: it's recorded with `status = 'failed'` and its error in
the DB. A target that does error is skipped along with what depends on it, and the rest of the
run continues (`error = "continue"`).

## Rebuilding the database

```r
targets::tar_invalidate(starts_with("db_")); targets::tar_make()
```

After a schema change, delete the DB and its `stability_artifacts/` first (the schema is
versioned and an old DB is refused). Nothing upstream reruns.
